_comment: Hand-computed normalisations. Each entry was worked out on paper from the printed figures and the rounding rules, then written here as exact rationals. They are not a snapshot of the tool's output; if the tool disagrees with one of these, one of the two is wrong and the test says which. The upper bound is exclusive throughout.

cases.why: 8 g of fat prints from [7.5, 8.5). A 55 g serving prints from [54.5, 55.5). Dividing the smallest fat by the largest serving gives 100 * 7.5 / 55.5 = 500/37, and the largest fat by the smallest serving gives 100 * 8.5 / 54.5 = 1700/109. The endpoints swap, which is the whole reason interval division is not two divisions.
230 kcal prints from [225, 235). 100 * 225 / 55.5 = 15000/37 and 100 * 235 / 54.5 = 47000/109. That is a 26 kcal spread on a figure most people would read as a single number.

160 mg prints from [155, 165). Eight servings prints from [7.5, 8.5) because servings above 5 go to the nearest whole. 155 * 7.5 = 1162.5 and 165 * 8.5 = 1402.5. Two roundings multiplied together give a 240 mg spread, which is a tenth of the daily value.

the headline case. 0 g of trans fat prints from [0, 0.5). A declared 2.5 servings prints from [2.25, 2.75) because counts between 2 and 5 go to the nearest half. 0.5 * 2.75 = 1.375 g, so a package labelled zero trans fat throughout can hold nearly a gram and a half of it.
asymmetric because the 2 to 5 mg band is reserved for the less-than-5 form, so a printed 5 mg cannot have come from 4.9 mg
declared per serving already, so no conversion applies and the interval is the bare rounding interval of 140 kcal above the 50 kcal breakpoint

100 * 135 / 34.5 = 9000/23 and 100 * 145 / 33.5 = 29000/67. Against cereal B's [15000/37, 47000/109) the two intervals overlap almost completely, while the per-serving figures differ by about 60 percent.

140 mg sits on the boundary where the step changes from 5 mg to 10 mg, so it prints from [137.5, 145). A 32 g serving prints from [31.5, 32.5). 100 * 137.5 / 32.5 = 5500/13 and 100 * 145 / 31.5 = 29000/63.
a liquid, so the basis reads per 100 ml. 150 kcal prints from [145, 155) and a 240 ml serving from [239.5, 240.5). 100 * 145 / 240.5 = 29000/481 and 100 * 155 / 239.5 = 31000/479.

declared per 100 ml already, so no conversion applies. 91.6 g is printed to a tenth of a gram, finer than the guidance step for figures above 10 g, so the interval comes from the printed precision: [91.55, 91.65).

0.12 g per 100 g prints from [0.115, 0.125). A 125 g pot prints from [124.5, 125.5). Scaling gives 0.115 * 1.245 = 5727/40000 and 0.125 * 1.255 = 6275/40000. The equivalent sodium figure is this divided by 2.5.
a printed 0 calories carries the whole below-5 allowance, so a can labelled zero can hold just under 5 kcal
